gate: A 65-parameter 6-to-8-tanh-to-1-sigmoid network mixes preceding fast and slow input/output cross-moment summaries. Its six inputs are log RMS of fast-minus-slow, fast and slow summaries; RMS of the current input mean; log lagged prediction error; and cosine between the two summaries. It sees no current output, true regime, boundary or task family. Zero output-layer initialization gives exactly a half mixture. Gate parameters persist across all changes in a stream.
learning: Compute and record the prequential prediction before observing outputs. Once noisy outputs arrive, differentiate that already-computed prediction loss through the student into gate parameters. Clip gate-gradient norm to one and apply Adam with rate 0.003 and betas 0.9/0.99. The student then takes the unchanged replay update using the detached prior context that produced the prediction. Fast and slow evidence summaries update from observed outputs. The gate is optimized for actual causal prediction, not context reconstruction or a training-only target summary. This is a local online gradient, not differentiation through all future student updates or recursive self-application.
controls: Use unchanged E17 slow/fast prior learners and E21 fast posterior assignment. Fixed mixture uses the same two summaries at weight one-half with no trainable gate. All students have 738 parameters, 512 replay examples and the same initial weights/data/RNG. No reset at boundaries. The learned gate must beat or improve the tradeoff against strong fixed alternatives, not merely the previously weak slow context.
worlds: The first two families use the unchanged E17 generator. Coupled and independent families use four nonlinear functions and four input means with separately seeded world, observation and schedule RNGs. Coupled changes both using one schedule; independent changes function and input index on independent 16-to-64-batch schedules. Alternating dependency adds 512-batch phases within the same lifetime: input changes continue, while the conditional function alternates between being held fixed and following its independent change schedule. It begins fixed and carries the last function across each fixed phase. The learner receives neither indices nor phase labels. Evaluation segments are the union of actual input/function changes; mark segments shorter than three batches because the frozen recovery criterion cannot complete there. Report them, do not discard their prediction errors or hide censoring.
evaluation: Record clean/noisy prequential error, quarters, all segments and E17 censored recovery. For gated arms record actual pre-output gate weights over time and every gate update. All updates/thresholds/seeds are frozen before scoring. No task-family labels or final data select a fixed comparator, train the gate offline or choose a checkpoint.
preflight: Verify old-family generator equality, truly independent change events, fixed controls' exact equality with their original classes, half-mixture initial equality, no current-output argument in prediction, finite-difference gate derivative, gate parameter changes from actual errors, bounded replay, exact resumed gate/student state and correctly charged extra backward work. New-world generation must preserve prefixes when extended.
costs: All model forwards, student and gate backward calls, gate inference, gate parameters and optimizer moments, both evidence summaries, replay, context, RNG state, serialized checkpoints and local runtime count. Reuse the recorded prediction graph for gate learning; do not add an uncounted student forward. Full autograd-intermediate peak memory, process RAM, complete FLOPs and energy remain unmeasured. There are 100 new learner runs on twenty paired worlds; repeated exposures are not independent data acquisition.
falsification: If the learned gate cannot match the appropriate fixed controls, simply adding a learned allocator has not repaired the timescale tradeoff. If gains disappear when input and function shifts are decoupled, it learned a family shortcut. Average gate movement and successful parameter updates are not evidence of improved learning. Any positive package gain still needs matched-state keep/revert gate continuation before claiming a persistently better procedure.
scope: A new implemented evidence-allocation component within the candidate architecture, using established filtering/gating/online-gradient ideas. No novelty, semantic compression, general reasoning, closed-loop control, recursive self-application or full goal-completion claim follows from this finite supervised test.
